# GeekNews HTML Structure Analysis

## Overall Page Architecture

The page is a news aggregation site with a clean hierarchical structure. Based on the provided content, here's how the main elements are organized:

## Key Structural Elements

**Header Navigation:**
- Main logo/home link: `[GeekNews](/)`
- Navigation menu with sections like `/new`, `/comments`, `/past`, `/ask`, `/show`, `/plus`, `/weekly`
- Authentication link: `/login`
- Write article button: `/write`

**Article List Structure:**
Each article entry follows this pattern:
- Vote button: `[▲](javascript:vote(ID, "up");)`
- Article title (linked): `[Title](URL)`
- Source domain in parentheses: `(domain.com)`
- Description snippet with formatting
- Metadata line: Points, author link, timestamp, comment count

**Example Article Element:**
```
[▲](javascript:vote(27513, "up");)
[Article Title](URL)(source.com)
[- Description text...](topic?id=27513)
Points by [username](/user?id=username) timeframe | [Comments](topic?id=27513&go=comments)
```

## Key CSS/JavaScript Features

- **Keyboard Navigation**: "J,K" hotkeys for browsing (implemented via `hotkeys()`)
- **Voting System**: `javascript:vote(ID, "up")` handlers
- **Pagination**: `/?page=N` parameter structure
- **Search**: `/search?q={search_term_string}` using URL parameters

## Footer Structure

- Multiple link sections separated by pipes `|`
- Resources: Start, Guidelines, FAQ, About
- Legal: Terms, Privacy
- Social: X, Facebook
- Bot integrations: Slack, Jandi, Discord, Teams, Dooray, Google Chat, Swit

The design prioritizes accessibility with clear topic IDs, user profiles, and discussion threading.

content.text: Based on my analysis of the three pages, here's what I found: ## Key Findings ### 1. **Main Page (https://news.hada.io/)** & **/new** Both pages have the same article structure: **Article Element Hierarchy:** ``` [▲] Vote button ↓ javascript:vote(ID, "up") [Article Title] (Linked) ↓ Links to /topic?id=ID (Source Domain) [Description/Summary text] ↓ Also linked to topic page Metadata Line: • Points count • [Username link] (/user?id=username) • Timestamp • [Comments link] (/topic?id=ID&go=comments) ``` **CSS/Markup Patterns:** - Vote element: `▲` - Article title: Standard `` tag linking to `/topic?id=ID` - Source domain: Shown in parentheses `(domain.com)` - Pagination: Uses `/?page=N` query parameter - Load more: Button labeled "토픽 더 불러오기" (Load more topics) ### 2. **Topics Page (https://news.hada.io/topics)** **Critical finding:** This page returns essentially "Nope" - meaning: - There is NO dedicated topics/categories page - Topic/category organization doesn't exist as a separate browsable section - All navigation is driven by the main feed ### 3. **Navigation Structure** The site uses a horizontal navigation bar with these sections: - `/new` - Latest articles - `/comments` - Recent comments - `/past` - Past articles - `/ask` - Q&A section - `/show` - Show/discussion section - `/plus` - Premium section (GN⁺) - `/weekly` - Weekly digest - `/login` - Authentication ### 4. **Scraper-Relevant Details** - **Article IDs**: Stored as query parameter `id=27513` (example) - **Links structure**: `/topic?id=ID` for articles, `/user?id=username` for authors - **Pagination**: Modify `?page=N` parameter (1-indexed) - **No robots.txt restrictions visible** - but check before scraping - **No visible CSS class names** - structure relies on semantic HTML and position - **No tags/topics metadata** visible in articles themselves The site is relatively simple with a clean, Hacker News-like design. There are no embedded topic tags within articles, only article titles and brief descriptions.
